name: Something Behind You
flavor: The oldest gag in the act, and it has never once stopped working: you look past their shoulder, and their whole body believes you before their mind gets a vote.
description: You put a single vivid, wrong thing at a creature's shoulder — a shape, a breath, a hand closing — and let its own nerves do the work. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw against your {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. On a failure it takes [[2d6]] psychic damage as the fright goes through it like a shock; on a success it takes half as much. This is plain, reliable damage with no rider attached — it always works the same way, which is exactly what it is for.
narration: Your eyes flick to a point just past their shoulder and your face does something honest. Whatever they turn to find is already gone, and the jolt of it hits them somewhere under the ribs.
sheetSummary: Wisdom save vs {{trick save DC|8 + proficiency bonus + your trick ability modifier}}. Fail: [[2d6]] psychic. Success: half damage. No rider.
